why: Counting multisets of weights 1..k with sum total is the coin-change-ways problem: each weight is a coin with unlimited supply. Looping weights in the outer loop counts combinations (not orderings).
hints: Order does not matter and each weight can repeat. This is a known 'number of ways to make change' problem.
ways[s] = number of combinations summing to s using the weights processed so far. Adding weight w: ways[s] += ways[s - w] for s from w up to total.
Initialise ways[0] = 1, loop w = 1..min(k, total) outside and s inside (ascending, since reuse is allowed), mod 1e9+7. O(total * k).
pitfalls: Swapping the loops (sums outside, weights inside) counts ordered sequences instead.
Weights larger than total never contribute; cap at min(k, total).
